questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Commerce is best defined as
options: all activities connected with the buying, selling, and distribution of goods and services
the manufacturing of goods only
the process of farming for domestic consumption
the extraction of raw materials from the earth
questions.explanation: Commerce covers trade (buying and selling) together with the aids to trade (like banking, insurance, and transport) that make the exchange of goods and services possible.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The two main branches of commerce are
options: import and export only
production and consumption
banking and insurance only
trade and aids to trade
questions.explanation: Commerce is broadly divided into trade (the actual buying and selling of goods) and aids to trade (services like banking, insurance, transport, and warehousing that support trade).

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Commerce is important to an economy mainly because it
options: eliminates the need for production entirely
prevents any form of international trade
bridges the gap between producers and consumers, ensuring goods reach those who need them
replaces the need for a legal system
questions.explanation: Commerce closes the gap between where goods are produced and where they are consumed, ensuring an efficient flow of goods and services to satisfy consumer wants.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the relationship between commerce and industry?
options: Industry only deals with services, not goods
Industry and commerce are entirely unrelated activities
Commerce produces raw materials for industry
Industry produces goods, while commerce facilitates their distribution and exchange
questions.explanation: Industry (production) creates goods, while commerce provides the trading and support activities needed to move those goods from producers to final consumers.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Direct services, as an aid to trade, refer to services rendered
options: only to manufacturing industries
only in international trade transactions
exclusively to the government
directly to consumers, such as those provided by doctors and teachers
questions.explanation: Direct services are personal services rendered straight to the final consumer (e.g., medical, educational, legal services), as distinct from commercial services that support trade.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Which of the following best illustrates the evolution of commerce from its earliest form?
options: Barter trade evolved into monetary exchange as economies grew more complex
International trade existed before local trade
Money was used before goods were ever exchanged
Modern e-commerce existed before the barter system
questions.explanation: Commerce historically progressed from simple direct exchange of goods (barter) to the use of money as a medium of exchange, enabling more complex and efficient trade.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The scope of commerce includes all of the following EXCEPT
options: trade (buying and selling of goods)
insurance services
the manufacturing process of converting raw materials into finished goods
banking services
questions.explanation: Manufacturing is part of industry (production), not commerce; commerce focuses on the exchange and distribution of goods, along with the services that support trade.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Commerce is related to other disciplines such as Economics mainly because both study
options: the physical properties of matter
how scarce resources are used to satisfy human wants through production, exchange, and consumption
the biological classification of organisms
only the political structure of a country
questions.explanation: Commerce is essentially a practical application of core economic principles concerning the exchange of scarce resources (goods and services) to satisfy consumer wants.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Occupations are broadly classified into which three categories?
options: Government, private, and foreign occupations
Skilled, unskilled, and volunteer occupations
Rural, urban, and suburban occupations
Industrial, commercial, and service occupations
questions.explanation: The standard classification of occupations in commerce studies divides them into industrial (production), commercial (trade and its aids), and service (direct personal services) occupations.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: An industrial occupation is one primarily concerned with the
options: extraction and production of raw materials and goods
distribution of goods to final consumers
buying and selling of finished goods
provision of personal services like teaching
questions.explanation: Industrial occupations include activities such as mining, farming, and manufacturing, focused on producing goods and raw materials rather than trading or servicing them.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A commercial occupation is one primarily concerned with
options: trade and the aids to trade, such as banking and transport
extracting raw materials directly from nature
providing direct personal services like medicine
manufacturing finished goods from raw materials
questions.explanation: Commercial occupations encompass those working in trade itself and the supporting services (banking, insurance, transport, warehousing) that facilitate the exchange of goods.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A service occupation is one primarily concerned with providing
options: wholesale distribution of goods
raw materials for manufacturing
direct personal services to individuals, such as those of a doctor or lawyer
warehousing facilities for goods in transit
questions.explanation: Service occupations involve rendering direct, personal services to consumers (e.g., healthcare, legal advice, teaching), distinct from producing or trading physical goods.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Which of the following is an example of an industrial occupation?
options: Insurance underwriting
Banking
Retailing
Mining
questions.explanation: Mining is a primary industrial activity involving the extraction of raw materials, unlike banking, retailing, and insurance, which are commercial or service activities.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a commercial occupation?
options: Farming
Nursing
Teaching
Wholesaling
questions.explanation: Wholesaling is a trading activity, forming part of commerce, whereas farming is industrial, and teaching and nursing are direct personal service occupations.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A sole proprietorship is a business owned and controlled by
options: two or more partners sharing profits equally
shareholders through purchased shares
a government agency on behalf of the public
one individual who bears all the risks and enjoys all the profits
questions.explanation: Sole proprietorship is the simplest form of business ownership, run by a single person who has full control, keeps all profits, but also bears unlimited personal liability for debts.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A major disadvantage of a sole proprietorship is that the owner has
options: no right to keep the profits made
no control over business decisions
to share profits with numerous partners
unlimited liability for the debts of the business
questions.explanation: Because the business has no separate legal identity from its owner, the sole proprietor's personal assets are at risk to cover business debts, a key disadvantage of unlimited liability.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A partnership is formed when
options: two or more persons agree to carry on a business together with a view to making a profit
the government establishes a public corporation
shares are sold to the general public
a single individual registers a company
questions.explanation: A partnership involves two or more people combining resources and expertise to jointly run a business for shared profit, typically guided by a partnership agreement (deed).

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A private limited liability company differs from a public limited liability company mainly in that a private company
options: cannot offer its shares for sale to the general public
must have at least seven shareholders
cannot have limited liability for its shareholders
is always owned by the government
questions.explanation: Private limited companies restrict the transfer of shares and cannot invite the public to subscribe for shares, unlike public limited companies, which can freely sell shares on the stock exchange.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Limited liability, a key feature of registered companies, means that shareholders' liability for company debts is limited to
options: the amount unpaid on the shares they hold
their entire personal wealth
double the value of their shareholding
nothing at all, even if shares are unpaid
questions.explanation: Under limited liability, a shareholder's financial risk is capped at the amount they invested (or still owe) on their shares, protecting their personal assets from business debts.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A cooperative society is a business organisation formed mainly to
options: promote the mutual economic interest of its members through joint effort
operate exclusively as a government-owned enterprise
trade only in agricultural produce
maximise profit for a single wealthy owner
questions.explanation: Cooperative societies are voluntary associations where members pool resources to achieve common economic goals, such as better prices for produce or accessible credit.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A public corporation is a business organisation that is
options: restricted from operating in any commercial sector
owned entirely by private shareholders
owned and controlled by the government to provide essential services
formed by two or more individuals for personal profit only
questions.explanation: Public corporations are established and owned by government to provide important services (e.g., utilities, transport) often considered too essential to leave solely to private enterprise.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A joint venture is best described as an arrangement where
options: two or more businesses combine resources temporarily to undertake a specific project
a company sells all its shares to a single buyer
a sole trader converts to a limited company
one business permanently absorbs another
questions.explanation: A joint venture is typically a temporary or project-specific partnership between separate businesses that pool resources and expertise to achieve a common commercial objective.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Which business unit is generally easiest and cheapest to establish, requiring minimal legal formalities?
options: Sole proprietorship
Public limited liability company
Joint venture between multinational firms
Public corporation
questions.explanation: Sole proprietorships have the fewest legal requirements for formation, making them the simplest and least expensive business structure to set up compared to companies or corporations.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Which of the following is a key advantage of a public limited liability company over a sole proprietorship?
options: Simpler and faster decision-making processes
Complete freedom from any government regulation
Ability to raise large amounts of capital by selling shares to the public
No requirement to publish annual financial statements
questions.explanation: Public companies can raise substantial capital by offering shares to the general public through the stock exchange, a scale of fundraising not available to a sole proprietorship.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Home trade refers to the buying and selling of goods
options: within the boundaries of a single country
exclusively through international shipping
only at government-approved international fairs
between two or more different countries
questions.explanation: Home (domestic) trade takes place entirely within a country's borders, as opposed to foreign trade, which involves the exchange of goods across national boundaries.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Wholesale trade involves the
options: exportation of goods to foreign countries
direct sale of goods in small quantities to final consumers
buying of goods in bulk from producers for resale in smaller quantities to retailers
manufacturing of goods from raw materials
questions.explanation: Wholesalers act as intermediaries who buy in large quantities from producers and break bulk, selling smaller quantities on to retailers rather than directly to final consumers.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Retail trade involves the sale of goods
options: exclusively between two countries
in bulk to other businesses for resale
in small quantities directly to the final consumer
only through cooperative societies
questions.explanation: Retailing is the final link in the distribution chain, selling goods in small, consumer-friendly quantities directly to the person who will use them.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The normal channel of distribution for many consumer goods follows the sequence
options: consumer to retailer to wholesaler to producer
producer to wholesaler to retailer to consumer
retailer to producer to consumer to wholesaler
producer to consumer to wholesaler to retailer
questions.explanation: This is the traditional distribution channel: goods move from the manufacturer/producer, through a wholesaler who breaks bulk, to retailers, and finally to the end consumer.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: E-commerce, a modern trend in home trade, refers to
options: a government policy restricting online transactions
trade conducted exclusively using physical cash
the buying and selling of goods and services over the internet
trade restricted only to wholesalers
questions.explanation: E-commerce represents a modern, digital channel of trade, allowing consumers and businesses to transact online without necessarily visiting a physical shop.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A supermarket is a modern retail outlet characterised mainly by
options: large-scale self-service retailing of a wide variety of goods under one roof
trade conducted exclusively between two countries
the sale of goods only in bulk to other retailers
door-to-door selling of a single product
questions.explanation: Supermarkets are large retail stores offering a wide range of goods on a self-service basis, a modern evolution from smaller, traditional specialist shops.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Foreign trade refers to the exchange of goods and services
options: exclusively among cooperative societies
within the same city only
between a wholesaler and a retailer domestically
between two or more different countries
questions.explanation: Foreign (international) trade involves the flow of goods and services across national borders, distinguishing it from home (domestic) trade.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Import trade refers to the
options: exchange of goods purely within the home country
trade conducted by a country with itself
purchase of goods and services from other countries into the home country
sale of home-produced goods to other countries
questions.explanation: Imports are goods and services brought into a country from abroad, representing an inflow of foreign-produced goods into the domestic market.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Export trade refers to the
options: sale of home-produced goods and services to other countries
purchase of foreign goods into the home country
the process of manufacturing goods domestically only
trade restricted to within a single country
questions.explanation: Exports represent goods and services produced domestically and sold to foreign buyers, an outflow of home-produced goods to other countries.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Entrepôt trade refers to the
options: purchase of goods for domestic use only
importation of goods into a country for subsequent re-exportation to a third country
exchange of goods without any use of money
sale of goods exclusively at wholesale prices
questions.explanation: In entrepôt trade, a country imports goods not for domestic consumption but to process, store, and then re-export them to another country, often profiting from its strategic trading location.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Which of the following is a common barrier to international trade?
options: Tariffs and import quotas imposed by governments
The complete absence of currency exchange rates
Universal use of a single global currency
Unlimited free movement of goods across all borders
questions.explanation: Tariffs (taxes on imports) and quotas (quantity restrictions) are common government-imposed barriers designed to protect domestic industries from foreign competition.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A Bill of Lading is a document used in foreign trade mainly to
options: serve as a form of local currency
serve as evidence of a contract of carriage of goods by sea and as a receipt for the goods shipped
calculate the exchange rate for a transaction
record a country's total balance of trade
questions.explanation: A Bill of Lading is a crucial shipping document that acts as a receipt for goods loaded onto a ship, evidence of the shipping contract, and often a document of title to the goods.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A Certificate of Origin, used in international trade, is a document that
options: certifies the country in which the exported goods were manufactured or produced
grants a company permission to operate domestically
records the exchange rate applied to a transaction
shows the total insurance value of a shipment
questions.explanation: A Certificate of Origin verifies where goods were actually made, which can affect the tariffs applied and eligibility for certain trade agreements or preferences.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A Bill of Entry is a document used mainly for
options: certifying the quality of manufactured goods
recording domestic retail sales transactions
declaring imported or exported goods to customs authorities
opening a bank account for a new business
questions.explanation: A Bill of Entry is a customs document detailing the goods being imported or exported, used by customs authorities to assess duties and monitor trade.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the function of a middleman in the channel of distribution?
options: Regulating the currency exchange rate
Facilitating the movement of goods from producers to consumers
Manufacturing goods from raw materials
Setting national trade policy for the government
questions.explanation: Middlemen, such as wholesalers and retailers, perform the essential function of bridging the gap between producers and final consumers within the distribution channel.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A Chamber of Commerce is an association formed mainly to
options: provide direct banking services to the public
manufacture goods for its member businesses
protect and promote the interests of businesses within a locality or industry
regulate the activities of the national government
questions.explanation: Chambers of Commerce serve as advocacy and support organisations for businesses, promoting trade interests, providing information, and sometimes resolving trade disputes among members.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Trade associations are generally formed to
options: act as a branch of government ministries
provide personal loans to individual consumers
compete directly against their own member businesses
represent and safeguard the common interests of businesses within a particular trade or industry
questions.explanation: Trade associations bring together businesses in the same industry to advocate for shared interests, set standards, and sometimes negotiate collectively with government or other bodies.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The Manufacturers' Association of Nigeria (MAN) primarily represents the interests of
options: foreign embassies in Nigeria
commercial banks operating in Nigeria
manufacturing industries in Nigeria
individual retail consumers
questions.explanation: MAN is the umbrella association representing and advocating for the interests of manufacturers and industrialists operating within Nigeria.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Export promotion councils are established mainly to
options: regulate the retail price of imported goods
encourage and support the growth of a country's export trade
provide healthcare services to exporters
restrict all forms of international trade
questions.explanation: Export promotion councils provide support, information, and incentives to help local businesses expand their exports and compete effectively in international markets.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Which of the following is a benefit of trade associations to their members?
options: Eliminating all competition among members entirely
Guaranteeing each member an equal share of the national market
Providing a collective platform to negotiate with government on industry-relevant policies
Directly setting the salaries of all employees in the industry
questions.explanation: Trade associations amplify their members' voices, allowing them to collectively engage with policymakers on issues like tariffs, regulations, and standards affecting the industry.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Corporate bodies such as the Nigerian Stock Exchange primarily facilitate
options: the manufacturing of industrial machinery
the direct retailing of consumer goods
the buying and selling of shares and other securities
international shipping of physical cargo
questions.explanation: Stock exchanges provide an organised marketplace where shares, bonds, and other securities of public companies can be bought and sold by investors.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A commercial bank is a financial institution primarily engaged in
options: printing the national currency
manufacturing consumer goods
accepting deposits and granting loans to individuals and businesses
setting national monetary policy exclusively
questions.explanation: Commercial banks serve as everyday financial intermediaries, accepting customer deposits and providing credit facilities (loans) to individuals and businesses.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The Central Bank of a country is responsible for
options: regulating the banking system and controlling the money supply
retailing consumer banking products in local branches
providing personal current accounts to individual customers
granting mortgages directly to homebuyers
questions.explanation: The central bank oversees monetary policy, regulates commercial banks, and manages the overall money supply, distinct from the day-to-day retail banking services of commercial banks.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A current account offered by commercial banks is mainly designed for
options: investment exclusively in company shares
holding foreign currency reserves for the government
frequent deposits and withdrawals, typically without earning interest
long-term savings that earn a high fixed interest rate
questions.explanation: Current accounts are designed for everyday transactions, allowing frequent withdrawals via cheques, cards, or transfers, usually without paying interest on the balance.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A savings account offered by commercial banks is mainly designed to
options: issue letters of credit for international trade
provide unlimited overdraft facilities
facilitate frequent daily large business transactions
encourage customers to save money while earning interest on their balance
questions.explanation: Savings accounts are intended for accumulating funds over time, typically offering interest as an incentive, though usually with some restriction on frequent withdrawals compared to current accounts.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A cheque is best described as a
options: certificate confirming ownership of company shares
government-issued currency note
type of loan given by a bank to a customer
written order instructing a bank to pay a specified sum of money to a named person or bearer
questions.explanation: A cheque is a negotiable instrument by which an account holder instructs their bank to pay a stated amount to the person or entity named on it.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: An overdraft is a banking facility that allows a customer to
options: earn a fixed high interest rate on savings
deposit money without any transaction charges
withdraw more money from their account than the actual balance, up to an agreed limit
obtain foreign currency without any exchange rate applied
questions.explanation: An overdraft is a short-term credit facility permitting an account holder to withdraw beyond their actual balance, up to a limit agreed with the bank, usually incurring interest.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Modern electronic banking services, such as ATMs and mobile banking, mainly benefit customers by
options: eliminating the need for any form of identification
replacing the need for a functioning central bank
providing convenient access to banking services without needing to visit a physical branch
guaranteeing free, unlimited loans to all customers
questions.explanation: Electronic banking channels like ATMs, mobile apps, and internet banking allow customers to perform transactions conveniently at any time, without physically visiting a bank branch.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: One key function of the Central Bank is to act as the
options: primary retailer of consumer electronics
banker to the government and lender of last resort to commercial banks
direct employer of all bank staff nationwide
sole insurer of all private businesses
questions.explanation: The central bank manages government accounts and provides emergency financial support to commercial banks facing liquidity shortages, acting as the lender of last resort.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Insurance is best defined as a system by which
options: individuals or businesses pay a premium to transfer the risk of potential loss to an insurer
banks guarantee unlimited loans to policyholders
the government provides free replacement for any damaged property
businesses avoid all forms of financial risk entirely
questions.explanation: Insurance allows individuals or businesses to pay a relatively small, regular premium to an insurer, who agrees to compensate them for specified losses, effectively pooling and transferring risk.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The principle of indemnity in insurance means that
options: the insured can claim any amount they wish regardless of the actual loss
insurance always pays out more than the value of the loss
the insured should be restored to the same financial position they were in before the loss occurred, no more and no less
premiums are refunded in full if no claim is made
questions.explanation: Indemnity ensures that insurance compensates the actual financial loss suffered, preventing policyholders from profiting from a claim beyond restoring their original position.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The principle of utmost good faith in insurance requires that
options: only the insurer needs to be truthful in the contract
both the insurer and the insured disclose all relevant material facts honestly
the insured can withhold any information they consider unfavourable
insurance contracts do not require any form of trust
questions.explanation: Utmost good faith (uberrimae fidei) obligates both parties to an insurance contract to disclose all material facts truthfully, since the insurer relies heavily on the insured's honesty in assessing risk.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Insurable interest, a fundamental principle of insurance, means that
options: only the insurance company needs to have an interest in the risk
anyone can insure any property regardless of ownership or relationship to it
insurable interest is only required for life insurance policies
the person taking out the policy must stand to suffer a genuine financial loss from the event insured against
questions.explanation: Insurable interest ensures the policyholder has a legitimate financial stake in the subject matter of the insurance, preventing insurance from being used as a form of gambling on unrelated events.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Life assurance differs from general insurance mainly in that life assurance
options: never requires payment of any premium
provides a certain payout since death is a certain event, unlike general insurance which covers uncertain events
is only available to business organisations
cannot be taken out on one's own life
questions.explanation: Because death is a certainty (only the timing is uncertain), life assurance guarantees an eventual payout, unlike general insurance (e.g., fire, motor), which only pays if the uncertain insured event actually occurs.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Fire insurance policies are specifically designed to compensate for losses arising from
options: damage caused by motor vehicle accidents
the death of a policyholder
damage to property caused by fire
theft of goods in transit
questions.explanation: Fire insurance specifically covers financial losses resulting from fire damage to insured property, distinct from other specialised policies like motor or marine insurance.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Which of the following is an importance of insurance to businesses?
options: It provides financial security against unforeseen losses, encouraging investment and risk-taking
It replaces the need for sound business management
It completely eliminates all business risks
It guarantees a fixed annual profit regardless of performance
questions.explanation: By transferring the financial burden of unpredictable losses to an insurer, insurance gives businesses the confidence to invest and take calculated risks they might otherwise avoid.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: An insurance premium refers to the
options: total value of the property being insured
amount of money paid periodically by the insured to the insurer for coverage
profit earned by an insurance company in a year
compensation paid by the insurer after a valid claim
questions.explanation: The premium is the regular payment the policyholder makes to the insurer in exchange for the promise of compensation should the insured risk occur.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Road transport is generally most suitable for
options: the fastest possible movement of goods over intercontinental distances
transporting extremely heavy bulk cargo across oceans
carrying goods that require no handling at all
short to medium distance movement of goods, offering flexibility and door-to-door delivery
questions.explanation: Road transport offers unmatched flexibility for door-to-door delivery over shorter to medium distances, though it is generally less efficient than rail or sea for very large or long-distance bulk cargo.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Rail transport is generally most suitable for
options: moving large quantities of bulky goods over long distances on land
very short distance local deliveries within a single street
delivering small parcels directly to individual homes
transporting goods across the ocean between continents
questions.explanation: Railways are well suited to carrying heavy, bulky cargo over long overland distances efficiently, though they lack the door-to-door flexibility of road transport.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Air transport, though generally the most expensive mode, is favoured mainly for
options: goods that have no time sensitivity at all
fast delivery of perishable or high-value, low-bulk goods over long distances
short local deliveries within a single city
transporting extremely heavy bulk raw materials cheaply
questions.explanation: Despite its high cost, air transport's speed makes it ideal for perishable goods (like flowers or fresh produce) and valuable, less bulky items needing urgent long-distance delivery.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Water (sea) transport is generally most economical for
options: moving goods across land-locked regions with no coastline
delivering goods directly to a customer's doorstep
moving very large volumes of bulky goods over long international distances
urgent same-day delivery of perishable goods
questions.explanation: Sea transport offers the lowest cost per unit for moving very large quantities of bulky cargo over long distances, though it is much slower than air transport.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A major disadvantage of road transport compared to rail transport is that road transport
options: is generally less suitable for moving very large quantities of bulky goods economically
cannot provide door-to-door delivery services
cannot be used to transport perishable goods
is always more expensive over any given distance
questions.explanation: While road transport offers unmatched flexibility, it is typically less cost-efficient than rail for transporting very large volumes of heavy or bulky goods over long distances.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Pipelines, as a specialised mode of transport, are mainly used to convey
options: passengers over long distances
solid manufactured goods like furniture
perishable agricultural produce
liquids and gases, such as crude oil, refined petroleum products, and natural gas
questions.explanation: Pipelines are specifically engineered to transport fluids (liquids and gases) continuously and efficiently over long distances, commonly used in the oil and gas industry.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Communication in commerce refers to the
options: extraction of raw materials from nature
storage of goods before they are sold
process of manufacturing goods for sale
process of exchanging information between businesses, customers, and other stakeholders
questions.explanation: Effective communication enables businesses to exchange essential information with customers, suppliers, employees, and other stakeholders, supporting smooth commercial operations.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Advertising is best defined as
options: the process of storing unsold inventory
a paid, non-personal form of communication used to promote goods, services, or ideas
the physical transportation of goods to the market
a free service offered by the government to businesses
questions.explanation: Advertising involves paying for media space or time to present a persuasive message about a product, service, or idea to a mass audience, without direct personal interaction.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The main function of advertising in marketing is to
options: manufacture goods for sale to consumers
inform, persuade, and remind consumers about goods and services
transport finished goods to retail outlets
provide direct personal financial advice to consumers
questions.explanation: Advertising works to create awareness (inform), influence purchase decisions (persuade), and reinforce brand recognition over time (remind) among target consumers.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a mass medium commonly used for advertising?
options: A face-to-face sales pitch to one customer
A personal handwritten letter
Television
A private telephone conversation
questions.explanation: Television is a classic mass medium capable of reaching a very large, broad audience simultaneously, making it a powerful (though costly) advertising channel.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Personal selling, as a promotional tool, differs from advertising mainly in that personal selling involves
options: communication that cannot be tailored to individual customer needs
direct, face-to-face interaction between a salesperson and a potential customer
no human interaction whatsoever
communication broadcast simultaneously to a mass, anonymous audience
questions.explanation: Personal selling is a direct, interpersonal promotional method, allowing tailored communication and immediate feedback, unlike the one-way, mass-audience nature of advertising.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Which of the following is an importance of advertising to producers?
options: It removes the need to consider consumer needs
It helps create brand awareness and can increase the volume of sales
It eliminates the need for a distribution channel
It guarantees that every consumer will buy the product
questions.explanation: Advertising helps producers build brand recognition and stimulate consumer interest, which can translate into higher sales volumes, though it does not guarantee purchases.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Warehousing refers to the
options: storage of goods from the time of production until they are needed for sale or use
transportation of goods between two countries
manufacturing of goods from raw materials
the process of insuring goods against loss
questions.explanation: Warehousing bridges the time gap between production and consumption by storing goods safely until they are required by wholesalers, retailers, or final consumers.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A bonded warehouse is a type of warehouse where
options: imported goods are stored without immediate payment of import duty until they are released for sale
only perishable goods can be stored
storage is provided completely free of charge
goods are stored exclusively for export
questions.explanation: Bonded warehouses allow importers to store goods under customs supervision, deferring the payment of import duties until the goods are actually released into the domestic market.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A private warehouse is one owned and used by
options: no one, as it is left permanently vacant
multiple unrelated businesses to store their varied goods jointly
the government for the storage of public goods only
a single individual or firm to store its own goods
questions.explanation: A private warehouse belongs to and serves the storage needs of one particular business, unlike public warehouses, which offer storage space to multiple different clients for a fee.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A public warehouse is one that
options: offers storage facilities for a fee to any business or individual needing space
is restricted only to government use
never charges any fee for storage services
is used exclusively by a single large corporation
questions.explanation: Public warehouses are commercial storage facilities available for hire by any business or individual, providing flexible storage space without the cost of building a private facility.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: One important function of warehousing is to
options: help stabilise the supply of seasonal goods by storing surplus for future use
eliminate the need for any form of transportation
guarantee an increase in the market price of stored goods
manufacture additional units of stored goods
questions.explanation: By storing surplus produced during peak seasons, warehousing helps ensure a more consistent supply of goods is available even during off-peak periods, stabilising availability and prices.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Cold storage warehouses are specifically designed to store
options: non-perishable manufactured goods only
goods intended exclusively for export
perishable goods that require refrigeration to prevent spoilage
documents and paper records
questions.explanation: Cold storage warehouses maintain low temperatures specifically to preserve perishable items like food products, preventing spoilage during the storage period.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Marketing can be defined as the process of
options: extracting raw materials for industrial use
storing goods indefinitely without selling them
manufacturing goods without regard to consumer needs
identifying, anticipating, and satisfying customer needs profitably
questions.explanation: Marketing focuses on understanding what consumers want and need, then delivering products or services that satisfy those needs while achieving business objectives such as profit.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The marketing mix, often called the '4 Ps', consists of
options: Product, Profit, Purchase, and Payment
Product, Price, Place, and Promotion
Planning, Pricing, Packaging, and Publicity
Production, Profit, People, and Process only
questions.explanation: The classic marketing mix framework identifies four controllable elements a business manages to market its offering effectively: Product, Price, Place (distribution), and Promotion.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: In the marketing mix, 'Place' refers to
options: the physical appearance and design of a product
the advertising and sales promotion activities used
the distribution channels and locations through which a product reaches consumers
the amount of money a customer pays for a product
questions.explanation: 'Place' in the marketing mix covers how and where a product is made available to consumers, encompassing distribution channels, logistics, and retail locations.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Market segmentation refers to the process of
options: eliminating competition from a particular market
dividing a broad target market into smaller groups of consumers with similar needs or characteristics
setting a single fixed price for all products
combining all consumers into a single, undifferentiated market
questions.explanation: Segmentation allows businesses to tailor their marketing efforts more effectively by grouping consumers based on shared characteristics such as age, income, location, or preferences.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Consumer protection is important mainly to
options: eliminate all forms of competition in the market
prevent any form of advertising by businesses
safeguard the rights and interests of consumers against unfair or harmful business practices
guarantee unlimited profit for producers
questions.explanation: Consumer protection measures and agencies exist to shield buyers from exploitation, unsafe products, and misleading practices, ensuring fair treatment in the marketplace.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The Consumer Protection Council (CPC) in Nigeria is primarily responsible for
options: regulating the stock exchange
setting the exchange rate of the naira
protecting consumers against harmful and hazardous products and unfair trade practices
manufacturing food and drug products
questions.explanation: The CPC works to safeguard Nigerian consumers from exploitative practices, unsafe goods, and violations of their rights as buyers of goods and services.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: NAFDAC (National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control) is primarily responsible for
options: controlling the prices of agricultural produce
regulating the banking sector
issuing business registration certificates
regulating and controlling the manufacture, importation, and sale of food, drugs, and related products
questions.explanation: NAFDAC ensures that food, drugs, cosmetics, and related regulated products meet safety and quality standards before they reach Nigerian consumers.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: SON (Standards Organisation of Nigeria) is primarily responsible for
options: collecting personal income tax
regulating food and drug safety exclusively
setting and enforcing quality standards for products manufactured or sold in Nigeria
managing the country's foreign exchange reserves
questions.explanation: SON develops and enforces national quality standards to ensure goods produced or sold within Nigeria meet acceptable levels of safety and quality.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Product branding in marketing is important mainly because it helps
options: guarantee the lowest price in the market
distinguish a company's product from those of competitors and build customer loyalty
eliminate the need for any product packaging
prevent a company from ever changing its product
questions.explanation: Branding creates a distinct identity for a product, helping it stand out from competitors and fostering repeat purchases through customer trust and loyalty.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Pricing strategy in the marketing mix must take into account which of the following factors?
options: The weather conditions on the day of sale
Production costs, competitor prices, and consumer purchasing power
Only the personal preference of the business owner
The colour scheme of the product packaging alone
questions.explanation: Effective pricing decisions balance the cost of producing a good, what competitors charge, and what target consumers are willing and able to pay.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Sales promotion, as an element of the promotional mix, typically involves
options: the manufacturing process of a product
long-term brand-building advertising campaigns only
short-term incentives such as discounts, coupons, or free samples to boost sales
the physical transportation of goods to retailers
questions.explanation: Sales promotions are typically short-term, tactical incentives (discounts, contests, samples) designed to generate an immediate boost in sales or encourage trial of a product.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A contract, in legal terms, is best defined as
options: a document issued only by government agencies
a legally binding agreement between two or more parties that is enforceable by law
a promise that has no legal consequences if broken
any informal conversation between two businesses
questions.explanation: A valid contract creates legally enforceable obligations between the parties involved, distinguishing it from a mere informal or social agreement.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Which of the following is an essential element required for a valid contract?
options: Physical presence of both parties at a bank
Offer and acceptance
Government approval for every transaction
A written document in every single case
questions.explanation: A valid contract generally requires a clear offer by one party and an unqualified acceptance by the other, along with other elements like consideration and intention to create legal relations.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Consideration, as an element of a valid contract, refers to
options: the age of the parties involved in the contract
something of value given by each party to the other as part of the agreement
the physical location where a contract is signed
the language in which a contract is written
questions.explanation: Consideration represents the value (money, goods, services, or a promise) exchanged between contracting parties, a key requirement for a contract to be legally binding.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: An agency relationship in business law exists when
options: one party (the agent) is authorised to act on behalf of another party (the principal)
a company issues shares to the general public
two businesses merge into a single company
a customer purchases goods directly from a manufacturer
questions.explanation: An agency relationship is created when a principal authorises an agent to act, negotiate, or transact on their behalf, legally binding the principal to the agent's authorised actions.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Under the law of sale of goods, a 'condition' in a contract of sale refers to a term that is
options: only applicable to contracts involving real estate
so fundamental that its breach entitles the injured party to terminate (repudiate) the contract
minor and only entitles the injured party to claim damages
irrelevant to the outcome of the contract
questions.explanation: A condition is a vital term of a sale contract; if breached, the innocent party may treat the entire contract as terminated, unlike a lesser term (warranty), which only allows a claim for damages.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A negotiable instrument, such as a cheque or bill of exchange, is a document that
options: cannot be transferred or assigned to another party under any circumstances
can be transferred from one person to another, conferring the right to receive payment
only functions as a form of identification
is legally binding only within a single company
questions.explanation: Negotiable instruments are transferable documents representing a right to a sum of money, and transferring them (e.g., by endorsement) passes on the right to receive that payment.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Management can be defined as the process of
options: manufacturing goods without any form of planning
planning, organising, leading, and controlling resources to achieve organisational goals
storing raw materials until they are needed
selling goods directly to final consumers
questions.explanation: Management involves coordinating an organisation's resources (people, materials, money) through the core functions of planning, organising, leading, and controlling, to achieve set objectives.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The planning function of management primarily involves
options: supervising employees during their daily tasks
setting objectives and determining the best course of action to achieve them
measuring actual performance against set standards
hiring and training new staff members
questions.explanation: Planning is the foundational management function, involving the setting of goals and deciding in advance the strategies and actions needed to achieve them.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The organising function of management primarily involves
options: setting the overall goals of the organisation
comparing actual results with planned targets
motivating employees to perform their tasks
arranging resources and tasks into a coherent structure to achieve set objectives
questions.explanation: Organising involves structuring the tasks, resources, and personnel of a business into a coordinated system designed to effectively carry out the plans that have been set.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The controlling function of management primarily involves
options: setting the initial objectives of the business
arranging the organisational structure of the firm
hiring new employees for the organisation
monitoring performance and taking corrective action where necessary to meet objectives
questions.explanation: Controlling closes the management cycle by comparing actual performance against planned targets and making necessary adjustments to keep the organisation on track.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A trader argues that 'commerce' and 'trade' are exactly the same thing. Why is this claim technically incorrect?
options: Trade only refers to international transactions, while commerce is purely domestic
Trade is the buying and selling of goods, while commerce also includes the aids to trade that make such exchange possible
Commerce is a narrower term restricted to banking and insurance alone
Commerce excludes wholesaling, which is classified under industry
questions.explanation: Trade is only one branch of commerce; commerce additionally embraces the aids to trade (banking, insurance, transport, warehousing, communication) that support the exchange of goods and services.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The historical shift away from barter was driven mainly by the difficulty of achieving a
options: double coincidence of wants between two trading parties
fixed exchange rate between two barterable goods
government-approved certificate of origin for each good
single global unit of account for all commodities
questions.explanation: Barter required each party to want exactly what the other offered at the same time (double coincidence of wants), a limitation money overcame by acting as a common medium of exchange.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Commerce is most closely linked to Economics because both disciplines fundamentally study
options: how limited resources are allocated to satisfy unlimited human wants
the legal procedure for registering a limited liability company
the geological formation of mineral deposits
the biological growth patterns of agricultural produce
questions.explanation: Commerce applies the core economic problem of scarcity, studying how resources are exchanged and distributed to satisfy consumer wants, making it a practical branch of economic activity.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A tailor who sews clothes for individual customers on request, and a bank that finances a textile exporter, are both classified as providing aids to trade, but under different headings, because the tailor renders a
options: extractive service, while the bank renders a manufacturing service
commercial service, while the bank renders a direct service
primary production service, while the bank renders a secondary service
direct (personal) service, while the bank renders a commercial service
questions.explanation: Direct services are personal services rendered straight to the consumer (like a tailor's), while commercial services such as banking specifically support and facilitate trade transactions.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Geography influences commerce mainly because a country's
options: national anthem determines which goods it can legally export
location, climate, and natural resources shape what it can produce and trade profitably
population size has no bearing on the volume of goods demanded
system of government automatically fixes its currency's exchange rate
questions.explanation: A nation's geographical features, climate, and resource endowment strongly determine its comparative advantage in production and, consequently, the pattern of goods it trades.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Which statement most accurately captures the evolution of commerce over time?
options: Trade progressed from localized barter and periodic markets to money-based exchange, and eventually to organized regional and global trading systems
Money was introduced before any exchange of goods took place between individuals
Modern retailing (supermarkets, e-commerce) preceded the establishment of local periodic markets
International trade blocs existed before local domestic markets were ever formed
questions.explanation: Commerce evolved in stages: from simple direct barter in local markets, to the adoption of money as a medium of exchange, and eventually to sophisticated regional and global trade arrangements.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A school leaver chooses a career based on expected income, job security, personal aptitude, and available training opportunities. These are all examples of
options: principles of insurance underwriting
elements of the marketing mix
factors determining the choice of occupation
barriers to international trade
questions.explanation: Choice of occupation is shaped by factors such as remuneration, security, aptitude/interest, training requirements, and social status, all weighed by the individual before settling on a career.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A furniture-maker who converts timber into finished chairs for sale is engaged in which type of occupation, distinct from the logger who fells the trees?
options: An extractive occupation, same as the logger
A commercial occupation, since furniture is eventually sold
An industrial occupation, but specifically a secondary (manufacturing) one
A service occupation, since furniture is a personal item
questions.explanation: Both are industrial occupations, but logging (extraction of raw timber) is primary production, while furniture-making (converting timber into a finished product) is secondary (manufacturing) production.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: An insurance broker who arranges cover between clients and underwriters, earning a commission, is best classified under
options: service occupation, because the broker deals with people directly
commercial occupation, because insurance is a recognised aid to trade
industrial occupation, because insurance involves processing risk
extractive occupation, because premiums are a form of raw material
questions.explanation: Insurance is one of the aids to trade, so those engaged in it (including brokers) are engaged in a commercial occupation, distinct from direct personal service occupations like medicine or teaching.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A cobbler who repairs shoes for individual customers, as opposed to a shoe factory that mass-produces footwear, is engaged in a
options: commercial occupation, while the factory is engaged in a service occupation
primary occupation, while the factory is engaged in a tertiary occupation
service occupation, while the factory is engaged in an industrial occupation
extractive occupation, while the factory is engaged in a commercial occupation
questions.explanation: Repairing shoes for individuals is a direct personal service, while mass production of footwear in a factory is an industrial (manufacturing) occupation.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Two graduates with identical qualifications choose different careers: one takes a lower-paying but highly stable civil service job, the other a higher-paying but volatile sales role. Their differing choices best illustrate that occupation choice depends on
options: government regulation forcing citizens into specific careers
the exchange rate of the national currency
only the amount of formal education completed
the trade-off individuals make between income level and job security
questions.explanation: Occupational choice often involves weighing multiple, sometimes conflicting factors such as income potential against the security and stability a role offers.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Of the four factors of production, the reward that specifically accrues to the entrepreneur for organising the other factors and bearing business risk is called
options: profit
interest
wages
rent
questions.explanation: While land earns rent, labour earns wages, and capital earns interest, profit (which can be negative) is the entrepreneur's reward for organising production and bearing the uncertainty of business risk.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: In a shoe factory, one worker only cuts leather, another only stitches, and a third only attaches soles, each repeating a single task all day. This arrangement is best described as
options: division of labour
diseconomies of scale
specialisation of industries
vertical integration
questions.explanation: Division of labour is the breakdown of a production process into separate, repetitive tasks, with each worker specialising in one stage, as illustrated by the shoe factory workers.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A region that concentrates entirely on producing cocoa, exchanging its surplus for other goods it does not produce, best illustrates
options: division of labour among individual workers
specialisation, which is division of labour applied at the level of regions or industries
the principle of insurable interest
entrepot trade between two coastal nations
questions.explanation: Specialisation extends the concept of division of labour beyond individual tasks to whole regions, firms, or industries concentrating on producing what they are best suited to.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A fisherman catching fish, a farmer harvesting cassava, and a miner extracting tin ore are all engaged in which stage of production?
options: Quaternary production
Secondary production
Primary production
Tertiary production
questions.explanation: Primary production involves the direct extraction or gathering of raw materials and natural resources from land, sea, or mines, as in fishing, farming, and mining.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A cassava processing plant that converts raw cassava tubers into garri, and a bakery that turns flour into bread, are both engaged in
options: extractive production only, not manufacturing
secondary production
primary production
tertiary production
questions.explanation: Secondary production involves transforming raw materials from the primary stage into semi-finished or finished goods, as with processing cassava into garri or flour into bread.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A logistics company that only transports and distributes already-manufactured goods to retailers, without producing anything physical itself, is engaged in
options: primary production
quaternary production only, as recognised in the JAMB syllabus
secondary production
tertiary production
questions.explanation: Tertiary production covers services that support the exchange and distribution of goods, such as transport, banking, and insurance, rather than the extraction or manufacture of physical goods.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A firm's factory building and machinery are classified as which type of capital, as distinct from the cash it uses to pay for daily raw material purchases?
options: Circulating capital, since machinery wears out quickly
Fixed capital, since these assets are used repeatedly over a long period
Working capital, same as the cash for raw materials
Loan capital, since machinery must always be financed by debt
questions.explanation: Fixed capital refers to durable assets like buildings and machinery used repeatedly over time, in contrast to working (circulating) capital, which is consumed or converted in the course of normal operations, such as cash for raw materials.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Land, as a factor of production, is distinguished from labour and capital mainly by the fact that its
options: reward is always called wages regardless of context
quantity increases automatically whenever population grows
productivity is entirely unrelated to its natural fertility
total physical supply is fixed and cannot be increased by human effort
questions.explanation: Unlike labour or capital, the total physical supply of land is fixed in nature and cannot be increased, though its usefulness can be improved through investment such as irrigation.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Excessive division of labour on an assembly line, where a worker repeats one tiny motion for years, can lead to which drawback often cited as a limitation of specialisation?
options: An automatic increase in the worker's wage each year
Monotony and boredom that can reduce worker morale and productivity over time
Complete elimination of unemployment in the economy
Guaranteed lifetime employment for the worker
questions.explanation: While division of labour boosts efficiency, a commonly cited disadvantage is that highly repetitive tasks can cause monotony, reducing job satisfaction and, over time, productivity.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A soft-drink vending machine that dispenses a bottle automatically upon payment, without any shop attendant present, exemplifies a modern retailing trend valued mainly for its
options: ability to extend selling hours and reduce the need for sales staff
requirement that customers must buy in bulk quantities only
function as a wholesale distribution centre
restriction to selling only imported goods
questions.explanation: Vending machines allow round-the-clock sales of standardised, low-value goods without staffing costs, making them a labour-saving innovation in modern retailing.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Self-service retailing, as practised in supermarkets, primarily reduces a retailer's operating costs by
options: increasing the amount of credit extended to customers
cutting down on the number of sales staff needed, since customers select goods themselves
requiring more sales assistants to guide each customer personally
eliminating the need for any product to be pre-packaged
questions.explanation: In self-service outlets, customers pick goods themselves from open displays and pay at a central checkout, allowing the retailer to operate with far fewer sales assistants than traditional counter service.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A retail business with several branches in different towns, all centrally owned, buying in bulk and selling under one common name, is best described as a
options: department store
cooperative retail society
hire purchase trader
chain (multiple) store
questions.explanation: Chain (multiple) stores are centrally owned and managed retail branches spread across different locations, benefiting from bulk buying while a department store is typically a single large building with many departments.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A wholesaler buys 500 cartons of soap directly from a manufacturer and subsequently sells them in smaller lots of 10 cartons each to different retailers. This function of splitting bulk quantities into smaller units is known as
options: consignment selling
under-invoicing
entrepot trade
breaking bulk
questions.explanation: Breaking bulk is a key wholesaling function, where large quantities bought from producers are divided into smaller, more manageable quantities suited to retailers' needs.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Under a hire purchase agreement, ownership of the goods transfers to the buyer only
options: immediately after the first instalment is paid
when the buyer resells the goods to a third party
the moment the agreement is signed, regardless of payment
after all the agreed instalments have been fully paid
questions.explanation: In hire purchase, the buyer merely hires the goods while paying instalments and only becomes the legal owner after the final instalment is paid, unlike an outright credit sale where ownership passes immediately.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Which feature distinguishes a department store from an ordinary chain (multiple) store?
options: A department store operates as a single large building housing many different sections under one roof, while chain stores are separate branches in different locations
A department store can only sell food items, unlike chain stores
A department store never offers credit facilities to customers
Chain stores are always owned by the government, unlike department stores
questions.explanation: A department store consolidates many different product departments within one large building, whereas a chain store operates multiple separate branch outlets, often smaller, in different locations under central ownership.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: An itinerant trader (hawker) contributes to home trade mainly by
options: taking goods directly to consumers in areas lacking fixed retail outlets
arranging international shipping documentation for exporters
underwriting insurance policies for small businesses
providing large-scale bulk storage facilities for manufacturers
questions.explanation: Itinerant traders move from place to place selling goods, extending retail distribution to consumers in remote or underserved areas without fixed shops.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A retailer who buys a consignment of umbrellas at the start of the rainy season and stores part of it to sell gradually as demand rises is performing which function associated with retail trade?
options: Breaking bulk only, and nothing else
Holding stock (warehousing) to bridge the gap between supply and steady consumer demand
Underwriting risk on behalf of the manufacturer
Acting purely as a re-exporter
questions.explanation: Retailers often hold stock to smooth out the timing gap between when goods are produced/acquired and when consumers actually want to buy them, a warehousing-type function within retailing.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A company in Country A imports raw cotton from Country B, spins and weaves it into finished cloth, and then sells the cloth to Country C. This is best described as
options: entrepot trade, since three countries are involved
ordinary import and export trade, not entrepot trade, because the goods are processed before re-sale
home trade, since the cloth is not sold domestically
re-export trade, since no value was added to the cotton
questions.explanation: True entrepot trade involves importing goods for re-export with little or no processing; because the cotton here is manufactured into cloth before being sold onward, this is ordinary trade (import then export), not entrepot trade.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A trading company in Singapore imports electronics from Japan and re-exports them unaltered to Nigeria, earning a margin without any manufacturing taking place. This is a classic example of
options: import substitution
dumping
entrepot (re-export) trade
counter-trade
questions.explanation: Entrepot trade occurs when a country imports goods purely to store, re-package, or re-export them to a third country without significant processing, often exploiting a favourable geographic or trading position.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A Bill of Lading differs from an Air Waybill mainly in that a Bill of Lading
options: cannot be used as evidence of a contract of carriage
typically serves as a document of title, allowing transfer of ownership of goods by endorsement, unlike a non-negotiable Air Waybill
is used only for goods transported by air, never by sea
is issued by an insurance company rather than a shipping line
questions.explanation: A Bill of Lading is usually a negotiable document of title (allowing the goods to be transferred by endorsement), while an Air Waybill is generally non-negotiable and only serves as a receipt and contract evidence.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A Consular Invoice is a document required by some importing countries mainly to
options: verify, through the exporting country's consulate, the value and origin of goods to prevent under-invoicing and assess correct duty
insure goods against loss in transit
grant the importer a loan for the transaction
record the shipping route taken by the vessel
questions.explanation: A consular invoice is certified by the consulate of the importing country stationed in the exporting country, helping to verify accurate values and prevent under-invoicing for customs duty purposes.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A Certificate of Origin differs from a Certificate of Inspection in that the former mainly certifies
options: the amount of import duty payable, while the latter certifies the bill of lading number
the insurance value of goods, while the latter certifies the buyer's creditworthiness
the country where the goods were manufactured, while the latter certifies that goods meet agreed quality/quantity standards before shipment
the exchange rate applied to the transaction, while the latter certifies the shipping route
questions.explanation: A Certificate of Origin confirms the country in which goods were produced (relevant for tariffs/trade agreements), while a Certificate of Inspection confirms that goods meet the agreed specifications and quality before shipment.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: An importer bringing in goods valued at N2,000,000, subject to a 15% import duty, would pay approximately how much in duty?
questions.explanation: 15% of N2,000,000 is N300,000 (2,000,000 x 0.15), representing the import duty payable on the consignment.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The balance of trade differs from the balance of payments in that the balance of trade covers only
options: invisible trade (services), while the balance of payments covers only visible goods
capital account transactions, while the balance of payments covers current account only
government-to-government loans, while the balance of payments covers private trade only
visible trade (physical goods), while the balance of payments covers both visible and invisible trade plus capital flows
questions.explanation: The balance of trade records only the value of physical (visible) exports minus imports, whereas the balance of payments is a broader record including invisible trade (services), income, and capital flows.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Compared to a tariff, an import quota restricts trade mainly by
options: taxing imported goods at a percentage of their value
subsidising domestic exporters directly
fixing a maximum physical quantity of a good that may be imported, regardless of price
banning all imports from a specific country permanently
questions.explanation: A quota is a direct quantitative restriction limiting how much of a good may be imported, whereas a tariff works indirectly by making imports more expensive through a tax rather than capping the quantity.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: An Export Processing Zone (EPZ) is established mainly to
options: restrict domestic firms from trading with any foreign country
offer incentives such as duty exemptions to firms producing goods primarily for export
ban all foreign investment within a country
regulate the retail price of goods sold within the home market
questions.explanation: EPZs are designated areas offering special incentives (like tax and duty exemptions) to attract firms that manufacture goods mainly intended for export, boosting a country's foreign exchange earnings.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: 'Dumping' in international trade refers to a practice where a country
options: refuses to export any goods to a rival trading partner
imports goods solely for re-export without any processing
imposes high tariffs on all imported raw materials
sells goods abroad at a price lower than that charged in its own domestic market, often below production cost
questions.explanation: Dumping occurs when a producer exports goods at an artificially low price (often below cost or below the home-market price), which can be damaging to competing industries in the importing country.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A currency devaluation is generally expected to make a country's exports
options: unaffected, since exchange rates have no impact on trade
more expensive and imports cheaper for foreign buyers
cheaper for foreign buyers, while imports become more expensive for domestic buyers
impossible to sell, since devaluation is a form of import quota
questions.explanation: Devaluation lowers the value of the domestic currency relative to others, making exports cheaper (and more attractive) to foreign buyers while making imports more costly for domestic buyers.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: At the port, a Bill of Entry is submitted to customs to declare imported goods, whereas a Bill of Lading is primarily
options: issued by customs authorities to calculate duty owed
a shipping document issued by the carrier, serving as a receipt for goods and evidence of the contract of carriage
a document confirming the exchange rate used for the transaction
used only for goods moving through a bonded warehouse
questions.explanation: A Bill of Entry is a customs declaration document, while a Bill of Lading is issued by the shipping company as a receipt for goods shipped and evidence of the carriage contract, serving distinct purposes in the same transaction.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A Letter of Credit used in international trade financing mainly serves to
options: replace the need for a bill of lading entirely
guarantee the exporter payment by the importer's bank once specified shipping documents are presented
provide personal accident insurance for the ship's crew
eliminate customs duties on the shipment
questions.explanation: A Letter of Credit is a bank's undertaking to pay the exporter once the exporter presents the agreed shipping documents, reducing payment risk in international transactions between parties who may not know each other well.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A merchant bank differs from a typical commercial bank mainly in that a merchant bank
options: only operates in the informal (unregulated) sector
focuses on wholesale banking services such as corporate finance and underwriting, rather than everyday retail deposits and withdrawals
is legally barred from lending money to any business
cannot accept any form of deposit from customers
questions.explanation: Merchant banks specialise in wholesale banking services like corporate finance, underwriting share issues, and advising businesses, in contrast to commercial banks which focus on everyday retail deposits, withdrawals, and personal loans.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A cheque crossed 'Account Payee Only' is designed mainly to
options: convert the cheque into a bearer negotiable instrument
ensure the proceeds are paid only into the bank account of the named payee, reducing the risk of fraud
allow the cheque to be cashed over the counter by any bearer
cancel the cheque permanently, preventing any payment
questions.explanation: Crossing a cheque 'Account Payee Only' restricts payment so that funds can only be credited to the named payee's own bank account, offering greater security than an open (uncrossed) cheque.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A bank draft differs from an ordinary personal cheque mainly because a bank draft is
options: never accepted for international payments
drawn by the bank itself on its own funds, making it more secure than a cheque drawn by an individual customer
only usable for withdrawing cash from a savings account
issued exclusively by the central bank to commercial banks
questions.explanation: A bank draft is issued and guaranteed by the bank against its own funds, making it more secure than a personal cheque, which depends on the drawer's account having sufficient funds.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: When a commercial bank grants a loan, it typically creates a corresponding deposit in the borrower's account, which can then be spent and re-deposited elsewhere in the banking system. This process describes
options: the function of a bonded warehouse
credit creation by commercial banks
the principle of utmost good faith
the entrepot trade cycle
questions.explanation: Credit creation refers to the way commercial banks expand the money supply by lending out a portion of deposits, with the loaned funds circulating and being redeposited, allowing further lending.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A discount house primarily specialises in
options: storing perishable goods for exporters
dealing in short-term money market instruments, such as discounting bills of exchange and treasury bills
underwriting long-term life assurance policies
retailing consumer electronics at discounted prices
