questions.explanation: Discount houses operate in the money market, specialising in buying and discounting short-term financial instruments like treasury bills and commercial bills, providing short-term liquidity to the financial system.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A standing order differs from a direct debit mainly in that a standing order
options: must be renewed physically at the bank branch every single month
is illegal in most banking systems worldwide
can only be used to receive money, never to pay it out
is an instruction from the account holder to the bank to pay a fixed amount at fixed intervals, while a direct debit allows the payee to vary and collect amounts owed
questions.explanation: A standing order is set up by the account holder to pay a fixed sum regularly, whereas a direct debit authorises the payee (e.g., a utility company) to collect varying amounts directly from the account as they fall due.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A customer notices a discrepancy between their own cash book balance and the bank statement balance due to unpresented cheques and uncredited lodgements. Resolving this discrepancy is done through a process known as
options: entrepot trade adjustment
bank reconciliation
underwriting
credit creation
questions.explanation: Bank reconciliation is the process of comparing and adjusting a firm's own cash book against the bank statement to account for timing differences like unpresented cheques and outstanding lodgements.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A development bank differs from a typical commercial bank mainly because a development bank
options: provides long-term capital for specific developmental projects, such as agriculture or industry, rather than everyday retail banking
only accepts short-term deposits withdrawable on demand
is prohibited from ever charging interest on any loan
operates exclusively outside the country of incorporation
questions.explanation: Development banks are specialised institutions providing long-term finance to support specific sectors of the economy (like agriculture, industry, or housing), unlike commercial banks which mainly offer short-term retail banking services.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A property owner takes out fire insurance on a warehouse he does not own and has no financial stake in. Even though he honestly discloses all facts to the insurer (satisfying utmost good faith), the policy is still void because it lacks
options: subrogation
insurable interest
indemnity
a cover note
questions.explanation: Insurable interest requires the policyholder to have a genuine financial stake in the insured property; honesty (utmost good faith) alone cannot validate a policy where no such interest exists, as this would amount to gambling.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: An insurance claim is rejected because the loss was found to have resulted from a cause not covered by the policy, even though a covered peril occurred earlier in the chain of events. This assessment relies on the principle of
options: utmost good faith
contribution
proximate cause
average
questions.explanation: Proximate cause requires identifying the dominant, most direct cause of a loss to determine whether it falls within the scope of perils covered by the policy.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: After compensating a policyholder for a car damaged by another driver's negligence, the insurer exercises its right to pursue the negligent third party for recovery. This right is known as
options: reinsurance
contribution
average clause
subrogation
questions.explanation: Subrogation allows an insurer, having paid a claim, to step into the insured's legal position and pursue recovery from the responsible third party, preventing the insured from profiting doubly from the same loss.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A warehouse is insured for the same risk with two different insurance companies. When a loss occurs, both insurers share the compensation proportionately rather than one paying the full amount. This illustrates the principle of
options: proximate cause
contribution
subrogation
insurable interest
questions.explanation: Contribution ensures that when the same risk is covered by more than one insurer, each shares the cost of a claim proportionately, preventing the insured from recovering more than the actual loss from multiple policies.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A trader insures goods worth N1,000,000 for only N600,000. If a partial loss of N400,000 occurs and the average clause applies, the trader will receive compensation of
options: N600,000, the full sum insured
N400,000 in full
N240,000, since the trader bears a share of the loss proportional to the under-insurance
N1,000,000, the full value of the goods
questions.explanation: Under the average clause, compensation is scaled down in proportion to the extent of under-insurance: (600,000/1,000,000) x 400,000 = N240,000, with the trader bearing the rest as a self-insured co-insurer.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: An insurance company that itself takes out a policy with another insurer to spread the risk of very large claims is engaging in
options: double insurance
entrepot insurance
reinsurance
co-insurance
questions.explanation: Reinsurance is the practice by which an insurer transfers part of its own risk to another insurer, protecting itself against unusually large or catastrophic claims.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Comprehensive motor insurance differs from third-party motor insurance mainly in that comprehensive cover additionally protects the
options: policyholder's own vehicle against damage, theft, and fire, in addition to third-party liability
government against loss of fuel tax revenue
third party's vehicle only, excluding the policyholder's own car
insurer against having to pay any claims at all
questions.explanation: Third-party insurance covers only liability for damage or injury caused to others, while comprehensive insurance additionally covers the policyholder's own vehicle against damage, theft, and fire.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A cover note issued by an insurer differs from the full insurance policy document in that a cover note
options: can only be issued after a claim has already been paid
is a permanent, final contract document that never expires
replaces the need for payment of any premium
provides temporary evidence of insurance cover pending the issue of the full policy document
questions.explanation: A cover note is a temporary certificate confirming that insurance cover is in force immediately, bridging the gap before the formal, detailed policy document is finalised and issued.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Containerization in sea transport has mainly improved international trade by
options: reducing handling time, damage, and pilferage of cargo during loading and transhipment
eliminating the need for any bill of lading
making it illegal to transport perishable goods by sea
restricting sea transport to only bulk liquid cargo
questions.explanation: Standardised containers can be moved quickly between ship, rail, and road without repeatedly unpacking goods, reducing handling costs, transit damage, and theft compared to loose cargo.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: 'Demurrage' in shipping refers to a charge imposed on
options: a charterer or consignee who fails to load or unload a vessel within the agreed free time, delaying its departure
an exporter for insuring goods above their market value
an importer who pays customs duty ahead of schedule
a shipping line for using containers instead of loose cargo
questions.explanation: Demurrage is a penalty charge levied when a ship is detained at port beyond the agreed free time due to delays in loading or discharging cargo, compensating the shipowner for lost time.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A freight forwarder's main role in international trade is to
options: underwrite marine insurance policies directly
act as an agent who organises the shipment, documentation, and customs clearance of goods on behalf of exporters or importers
set the exchange rate for cross-border transactions
manufacture goods on behalf of an exporter
questions.explanation: Freight forwarders act as specialist agents who coordinate the logistics, documentation, and customs processes involved in moving goods internationally, on behalf of traders who may lack this expertise.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Postal services and telecommunications both aid trade through communication, but they differ mainly in that postal services
options: cannot be used for any commercial correspondence
are entirely electronic, while telecommunications rely solely on physical delivery
have been made completely obsolete by e-commerce
primarily involve the physical conveyance of letters and parcels, while telecommunications transmit information electronically
questions.explanation: Postal services physically deliver letters, documents and parcels, whereas telecommunications (phone, internet, etc.) transmit information electronically and instantaneously, though both serve the communication needs of commerce.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A warehouse receipt issued for goods deposited in a warehouse can be useful to a trader mainly because it
options: grants the trader exemption from paying import duty
replaces the need for a bill of lading in all circumstances
can be used as collateral to obtain a loan from a bank, since it evidences ownership of stored goods
automatically insures the goods against fire
questions.explanation: A warehouse receipt evidencing goods held in store can be pledged as security, allowing a trader to raise short-term finance from a bank against the value of the stored goods.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Tourism is often classified in trade statistics as an 'invisible export' mainly because it
options: involves the physical shipment of tangible goods across borders
always results in a trade deficit for the host country
is exclusively a government-run activity with no private sector role
earns foreign exchange for the host country through services rendered to foreign visitors, without any physical good crossing the border
questions.explanation: Tourism brings in foreign exchange as visitors spend on services like accommodation, food and entertainment, similar to an export, yet no physical/tangible good is shipped abroad, making it an invisible export.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Multimodal transport in international trade refers to the movement of goods
options: exclusively by a single mode, such as road transport alone
only within the boundaries of one country
under a single contract, using two or more different modes of transport (e.g., sea, rail, and road) in one continuous journey
solely through pipelines regardless of the type of cargo
questions.explanation: Multimodal transport combines two or more transport modes under a single contract of carriage, allowing seamless movement of cargo, for instance from ship to rail to road, without separate contracts for each leg.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A charter party is a document that
options: sets out the contract terms when a shipowner hires out an entire ship or part of it to a charterer for a voyage or period of time
certifies the country of origin of goods being shipped
grants a warehouse operator the right to sell unclaimed goods
evidences ownership of shares in a shipping company
questions.explanation: A charter party is the contract between a shipowner and a charterer (who hires the vessel), specifying terms such as the route, duration, and freight charges for use of the ship.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Under an FOB (Free on Board) contract, as distinct from a CIF (Cost, Insurance, Freight) contract, the seller's responsibility for the goods generally ends once the goods
options: are manufactured, regardless of shipment
arrive at the buyer's final warehouse
pass the ship's rail at the port of shipment, after which the buyer bears freight and insurance costs
are cleared through the buyer's home customs
questions.explanation: Under FOB terms, the seller's obligation ends once goods are loaded onto the ship at the port of shipment; under CIF, by contrast, the seller additionally arranges and pays for freight and insurance to the destination port.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A partnership deed typically specifies all of the following EXCEPT the
options: amount of capital each partner is to contribute
proportion in which partners will share profits and losses
individual retail prices to be charged for every product sold nationwide by unrelated competitors
procedure for admitting a new partner or dissolving the partnership
questions.explanation: A partnership deed governs the internal relationship among the partners themselves (capital, profit-sharing, admission/dissolution procedures), not the pricing decisions of unrelated, competing businesses.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A sleeping (dormant) partner in a partnership is one who
options: is legally excluded from sharing in the firm's profits
takes no active part in managing the business but still contributes capital and shares in profits and liability
is actively involved in daily management but contributes no capital at all
has no liability whatsoever for the debts of the firm
questions.explanation: A sleeping partner invests capital and shares in the risks/profits of the business but does not participate in its day-to-day management, unlike an active (general) partner.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The Memorandum of Association of a registered company differs from its Articles of Association mainly in that the Memorandum
options: governs the internal management and day-to-day rules of the company
is optional and never required for company registration
defines the company's relationship with the outside world, including its name, objectives, and registered office
lists the names of all customers the company intends to serve
questions.explanation: The Memorandum of Association defines the company's external relationship with the public (name, objects, registered office, capital), while the Articles of Association set out the internal rules governing management and shareholder relations.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A company has an authorised share capital of N10,000,000, has issued shares worth N7,000,000 to shareholders, but has so far only received N5,000,000 in actual cash payment for those shares. The N5,000,000 already received represents the company's
options: issued capital
uncalled capital only, with no other classification
authorised capital
paid-up capital
questions.explanation: Paid-up capital is the portion of issued capital that shareholders have actually paid in cash, as distinct from authorised capital (the maximum the company may issue) and issued capital (shares actually allotted).

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A trading business records a total turnover (sales revenue) of N8,000,000 for the year. If its cost of goods sold and total operating expenses amount to N6,500,000, its net profit for the year is
questions.explanation: Net profit is turnover minus total costs and expenses: N8,000,000 minus N6,500,000 equals N1,500,000; turnover alone is not the same as profit.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A debenture differs fundamentally from an ordinary share in that a debenture holder is a
options: government regulator overseeing the company's operations
part-owner of the company entitled to vote at general meetings
creditor of the company entitled to fixed interest, regardless of whether the company makes a profit
shareholder entitled only to residual profits after all other claims are settled
questions.explanation: A debenture represents a loan to the company, so its holder is a creditor entitled to fixed interest payments regardless of profitability, unlike a shareholder, who is a part-owner with variable dividend entitlement dependent on profits.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A preference share differs from an ordinary share mainly in that a preference shareholder
options: is legally classified as a creditor rather than a part-owner
always receives a higher dividend than ordinary shareholders in a highly profitable year
has a prior claim to a fixed dividend before ordinary shareholders are paid anything
has greater voting rights than an ordinary shareholder at general meetings
questions.explanation: Preference shareholders receive a fixed dividend and are paid before ordinary shareholders, but typically forgo the higher (variable) returns ordinary shareholders may enjoy in a very profitable year, and usually have limited or no voting rights.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A cooperative society's principle of 'one member, one vote', regardless of the size of a member's shareholding, mainly distinguishes it from a
options: partnership, where votes are always distributed equally by law
sole proprietorship, where the single owner naturally has full control
public limited company, where voting power is generally proportional to the number of shares held
public corporation, which has no shareholders at all
questions.explanation: Unlike a public limited company where voting power typically depends on the number of shares owned, a cooperative society upholds democratic control by giving every member an equal vote regardless of their financial contribution.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A public corporation differs from a public limited liability company mainly in that a public corporation is
options: prohibited from employing any staff
always smaller in size than a typical private company
wholly owned and financed by the government to provide a public service, rather than owned by private shareholders seeking profit
financed exclusively through the sale of shares on the stock exchange
questions.explanation: A public corporation is a state-owned enterprise established to provide essential services, financed mainly by government, whereas a public limited company is owned by private shareholders who buy its shares on the stock exchange.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Because an ordinary partnership generally has unlimited liability, if the partnership's assets of N2,000,000 are insufficient to cover its debts of N3,500,000, the partners are legally required to
options: walk away, since the partnership is a separate legal entity
cover the shortfall of N1,500,000 from their own personal assets
ask the government to write off the debt entirely
convert automatically into a limited liability company to avoid payment
questions.explanation: Under unlimited liability, if a partnership's business assets cannot cover its debts, the partners must make up the shortfall from their personal assets, a key risk of this business form.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A franchise arrangement allows a franchisee to
options: become an unrestricted owner of the franchisor's entire company
avoid ever paying any fee to the franchisor
operate a business using an established brand name, products, and business model in exchange for fees paid to the franchisor
trade under a completely new, unrelated brand name of their own choosing
questions.explanation: In franchising, the franchisee pays fees for the right to trade using the franchisor's established brand, products, and proven business methods, while the franchisor retains overall brand ownership.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A holding company's relationship to its subsidiary is best described as one where the holding company
options: is legally merged into a single indistinguishable entity with the subsidiary
must always own exactly 100% of the subsidiary's total shares
owns a controlling interest in the subsidiary's shares, giving it power to influence or control the subsidiary's policies
has no financial interest whatsoever in the subsidiary
questions.explanation: A holding company owns enough shares (a controlling interest, not necessarily 100%) in another company (the subsidiary) to control its board and major policy decisions, while both remain separate legal entities.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A registered company may be compulsorily wound up (liquidated) by court order mainly when it
options: is unable to pay its debts as they fall due, among other statutory grounds
changes its registered trading name
declares a dividend higher than the previous year
increases its authorised share capital through a rights issue
questions.explanation: Inability to pay debts as they become due is one of the principal statutory grounds on which a court may order the compulsory winding up (liquidation) of a company.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The primary market for securities differs from the secondary market mainly in that the primary market deals with
options: the sale of newly issued securities directly by companies to raise fresh capital
only government treasury bills, never company shares
the resale of previously issued shares between existing investors
shares that have already been delisted from the exchange
questions.explanation: The primary market is where new securities are issued and sold for the first time to raise fresh capital, while the secondary market (like the stock exchange trading floor) facilitates subsequent trading of already-issued securities among investors.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: The Second-Tier Securities Market (SSM) was specifically established to enable
options: the complete elimination of stockbrokers from securities trading
the government to sell treasury bills exclusively
only long-established multinational companies to raise additional capital
smaller and medium-sized companies, unable to meet full listing requirements, to raise capital through the stock exchange
questions.explanation: The SSM offers relaxed listing requirements compared to the main market, giving smaller and growing companies that cannot meet the full listing criteria access to capital through the stock exchange.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A 'bull market' on a stock exchange describes a period when
options: trading on the exchange is suspended entirely
share prices are generally rising, and investor sentiment is optimistic
only government bonds may be traded
share prices are generally falling, and investor sentiment is pessimistic
questions.explanation: A bull market refers to a sustained period of rising share prices, driven by optimistic investor sentiment, in contrast to a bear market, which is characterised by falling prices and pessimism.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A rights issue allows a company to raise additional capital by
options: giving away shares completely free to the general public
borrowing money exclusively from a single commercial bank
offering new shares first to existing shareholders, usually at a discounted price, in proportion to their current holdings
converting all its ordinary shares into debentures
questions.explanation: In a rights issue, a company offers existing shareholders the right to buy new shares, usually at a discount and in proportion to their current shareholding, before the shares are offered more widely.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A bond is similar to a debenture in that both represent
options: profit-sharing instruments with no fixed return
ownership stakes entitling the holder to vote at company meetings
shares that can never be transferred to another investor
a form of debt/loan capital on which the issuer pays fixed interest to the holder
questions.explanation: Both bonds and debentures are debt instruments representing a loan to the issuer (company or government), obliging the issuer to pay fixed interest, unlike shares which represent ownership.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A bonus (scrip) issue of shares involves a company
options: capitalising part of its reserves to issue additional free shares to existing shareholders in proportion to their holdings
converting ordinary shares into government treasury bills
selling brand new shares to the public for cash at market price
buying back and cancelling shares already held by investors
questions.explanation: A bonus issue converts accumulated reserves into additional shares distributed free to existing shareholders in proportion to their current holdings, without requiring any new cash payment from them.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: An investor who spreads funds across shares in several different companies and sectors, rather than a single stock, is practising
options: insider trading
underwriting
entrepot investment
portfolio diversification, mainly to reduce overall investment risk
questions.explanation: Diversification spreads investment across multiple securities or sectors so that poor performance in one holding is offset by others, reducing the investor's overall risk exposure.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A stockbroker's main function on the stock exchange is to
options: insure investors against any loss of share value
set the official exchange rate of the national currency
manufacture the shares that companies issue
act as an agent who buys and sells securities on behalf of clients (investors), earning a commission
questions.explanation: Stockbrokers act as licensed intermediaries who execute buy and sell orders for securities on behalf of their clients, in return for a commission, since individual investors typically cannot trade directly on the exchange floor.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A company that groups its target customers by age, income, and family size, rather than by geographic region alone, is applying which basis of market segmentation?
options: Behavioural segmentation exclusively
Demographic segmentation
Geographic segmentation only
No segmentation, since all customers are treated identically
questions.explanation: Demographic segmentation divides a market according to measurable population characteristics such as age, income, gender, and family size, distinct from geographic (location-based) or psychographic (lifestyle-based) segmentation.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A product experiencing rapidly rising sales, growing competition, and the need for extensive promotion to build brand preference is most likely in which stage of the product life cycle?
options: Introduction stage
Decline stage
Growth stage
Maturity stage
questions.explanation: The growth stage is marked by rapidly increasing sales as the product gains market acceptance, attracting competitors, requiring strong promotional efforts to build brand preference over rivals.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A company launching a genuinely innovative product sets a very high initial price to maximise revenue from early adopters before gradually lowering it. This pricing strategy is known as
options: cost-plus pricing
loss-leader pricing
penetration pricing
price skimming
questions.explanation: Price skimming involves setting a high initial price to capture maximum revenue from customers willing to pay a premium, before gradually reducing the price to attract more price-sensitive segments.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A firm setting a deliberately low initial price to quickly gain market share and discourage competitors from entering is using
options: prestige pricing
penetration pricing
price skimming
psychological pricing only
questions.explanation: Penetration pricing sets an initially low price to rapidly build market share and customer base, often to establish a strong market position before potentially raising prices later.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Below-the-line promotion differs from above-the-line promotion mainly in that below-the-line activities
options: are illegal in most commercial jurisdictions
involve more direct, targeted promotional tools like sales promotions, direct mail, and point-of-sale displays rather than mass media
rely on mass media advertising, such as television and radio, to reach a broad audience
can never be measured for effectiveness
questions.explanation: Below-the-line promotion uses direct, targeted techniques (sales promotions, direct mail, exhibitions) aimed at specific audiences, in contrast to above-the-line promotion, which uses mass media advertising to reach a broad, general audience.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A firm launches a new product in a limited regional market before a full national rollout, in order to gauge consumer reaction and refine the marketing mix. This practice is known as
options: price skimming
product positioning
test marketing
market segmentation
questions.explanation: Test marketing involves trialing a product in a small, representative market to assess consumer response and adjust the marketing strategy before committing to a full-scale launch.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: Effective after-sales customer service (e.g., handling complaints, offering warranties) contributes to marketing success mainly by
options: replacing the need for any pricing strategy
guaranteeing that a product will never be returned
building customer satisfaction and loyalty, encouraging repeat purchases
eliminating the need for product quality control during manufacturing
questions.explanation: Strong after-sales service builds trust and satisfaction, increasing the likelihood that customers return for repeat purchases and recommend the brand to others, reinforcing long-term marketing success.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: When a business deliberately creates a distinct image for its product in the consumer's mind relative to competing brands (for example, as the 'premium' or 'budget' option), it is engaging in
options: entrepot marketing
product positioning
breaking bulk
market skimming
questions.explanation: Positioning refers to the deliberate effort to shape how consumers perceive a product relative to competitors, often emphasising a specific attribute, price tier, or brand image.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: E-commerce differs from the broader concept of e-business mainly in that e-commerce refers specifically to
options: a form of barter trade using digital tokens
all internal digital processes of a company, including HR and internal communication
the buying and selling of goods and services over electronic networks such as the internet
the manufacturing of computer hardware
questions.explanation: E-commerce narrowly refers to online buying and selling transactions, while e-business is the broader term covering all digital processes a company runs online, including internal operations, supply chain, and customer relationship management.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: E-banking (electronic banking) primarily allows customers to
options: print their own physical currency notes at home
eliminate the central bank's regulatory oversight of commercial banks
perform banking transactions such as transfers and bill payments electronically, without visiting a physical branch
avoid ever needing a bank account
questions.explanation: E-banking channels (internet banking, mobile apps, ATMs) let customers carry out transactions like transfers, balance inquiries, and bill payments remotely, without needing to visit a bank branch in person.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: In computing terminology relevant to commerce, 'bandwidth' most accurately refers to
options: the physical size of a computer's hard drive
the number of employees a company has trained in ICT
the total value of goods sold through an online store
the maximum rate of data that can be transmitted over an internet connection in a given time
questions.explanation: Bandwidth measures the capacity of a network connection to transmit data within a given period, which directly affects the speed and reliability of online transactions and e-commerce platforms.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A major challenge that can undermine consumer confidence in e-commerce transactions is
options: the elimination of physical retail stores worldwide
concerns over the security of online payments and protection of personal financial data
excessive availability of product reviews
the requirement that all online stores must operate 24 hours a day
questions.explanation: Because e-commerce transactions involve transmitting sensitive payment and personal data online, concerns about fraud, hacking, and data security are major factors that can deter consumers from shopping online.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.text: A 'firewall' in the context of ICT security for online commercial platforms is best described as
options: a software or hardware system that monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic to protect against unauthorised access
a legal document authorising an online business to trade internationally
a type of insurance policy covering fire damage to computer equipment
a physical warehouse used to store flammable goods
questions.explanation: A firewall is a network security system, either software or hardware based, that filters traffic between a trusted internal network and external networks to block unauthorised access and cyber threats.
